newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech O/N rates down amid repo hike fears-dealer.
newsitem.headline: Czech O/N rates down amid repo hike fears-dealer.

text.p: Overnight rates on the Czech money market fell on Friday morning as banks were reluctant to put funds on longer deposits, fearing that the repo rate could go higher soon, a dealer said.
David Poupe of Komercni Banka said overnight rates fell to as low as just over nine percent, but rebounded to around 10.0/10.5 percent by 0900 GMT, after an average spread of 12.24/12.50 on Thursday.

"There is a surplus (on the overnight market), and also a lack of confidence, despite the fact that the repo was done for a week. I think there is some distrust among banks that the repo might not be 12.9 percent tomorrow but higher," said David Poupe of Komercni Banka.
"Banks would rather place money for one day rather than placing it for a week at a fixed rate when tomorrow the (repo) could go some half a percent higher," he added.
The Czech National Bank held two one-week repo tenders with maximum yields set at 12.9 percent, up from the previous 12.4 percent.
After months of having a stable repo rate, the central bank said on Thursday that it would begin to set rates according to market conditions.
Poupe said one week to one month rates were at about 13.0/13.3 percent.
He said the market for long term money, from one month to one year, was highly illiquid.
"Nobody wants to be active on our market and put money here so liquidity is very low."
